newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures end lower on weaker dollar.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures end lower on weaker dollar.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures closed lower on Monday, as the yen's steep gains against the dollar offset the stronger Chicago market on Friday, traders said.
Prices were 170 yen to 400 yen lower, with the benchmark January 1998 contract down 180 yen at 15,530 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 45,505 lots.
The dollar fell as low as 120.30 yen in Asia earlier on Monday in reaction to the Saturday's Group of Seven statement.
"The yen's gains triggered active selling by local investors," a trader said. The Tokyo corn market will be closed on Tuesday for a national holiday.
The spot March contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.71-3/4 per bushel at 0805 GMT, against $2.71 at Friday's close.
The spot March of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.37-1/2 at 0805 GMT, down from $7.38 at Friday's close.
